scope: Independent implementation-facts review and direct visual inspection of the listed still frames with view_image. This does not certify full video playback or audio.
verifiedClaims: Random rental offer contains six Pokemon; the player selects three.
The opponent team is visible before battle; the player selects the lead each floor.
Factory uses single battles with three Pokemon per side and a random AI team.
A victory allows one optional exchange with the immediately previous opponent team.
Skipping the exchange advances the floor while preserving the current party.
Rankings show up to ten records with final Pokemon, held items and move names.
Global rankings use one best result per trainer; equal floors sort by earlier record.

findings.detail: Factory and ending title cards have readable large text and no title or game-address clipping.
Rental, lead and exchange screenshots contain all six cards or both three-Pokemon groups and their relevant action buttons.
Climb frames show floor 2 completion followed by floor 3 readiness; the skip-exchange action is visible.
Expanded ranking source screenshot shows all three final Pokemon, held items and four moves each.

Ranking footage was changed to a fixed 1.25 scale at centerY 0.48 after a readability recommendation. TOP 10 and the team row remain inside the image. Part of the bottom personal-record footer is cropped; this is outside the featured team-detail content.
Actual 2-second overlay frames for rentals, rankings and battle have legible two-line headings, sufficient contrast and no heading clipping. Four-second scene samples no longer contain the overlay.
The README and credits identify the local capture ranking as filming data rather than production rankings or audience metrics.
